name: Motivation Layer
description: Captures why the system exists: stakeholders and their drivers, assessments, goals and outcomes, principles, requirements and constraints, and the meaning and value attached to them (ArchiMate 3.2 motivation elements). Motivation elements are expressed in documents, decision records and requirement text rather than in executable code; every lower layer should be traceable back to an element here. Modelling rules: realization runs through motivation, as in ArchiMate: requirements realize the outcomes, goals and principles they make concrete, and outcomes realize goals. Decomposition is same-type only: an element aggregates the narrower elements of its own type that make it up, and specializes a more general one. Influence is one motivation element shaping another: drivers, assessments, stakeholders, goals, principles and constraints influence goals, outcomes, principles, requirements and constraints, and a constraint constrains the requirements it limits. Association is kept for concerns and interpretation: a stakeholder is associated with the drivers, goals, requirements, principles, outcomes and constraints it cares about, an assessment with the drivers it evaluates, and meaning and value are associated with any concept and are always the source of that association. Other layers trace to motivation with one predicate per meaning: they satisfy requirements, constraints and principles; an element realizes a goal or outcome it exists to achieve and supports one it contributes to alongside others; services and features deliver value, and user workflows deliver the outcomes they produce. A stakeholder is not served: business actors and roles, like personas, reference the stakeholder whose concerns they stand for.
